Express $\sin(x-\pi)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$ Enter the coefficient of each term, including zero if a term vanishes.

$\sin(x-\pi)=$ {{field-1}} $\sin x+$ {{field-2}} $\cos x$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u-v)=\sin u\cos v-\cos u\sin v.
$$

With $u=x$ and $v=\pi,$ use $\cos\pi=-1$ and $\sin\pi=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x-\pi)&=\sin x\cos\pi-\cos x\sin\pi\\
&=\sin x\cdot(-1)-\cos x\cdot 0\\
&=-\sin x\\
&=(-1)\sin x+0\cos x.
\end{aligned}
$$

The requested coefficients are $-1$ and $0,$ in that order.

questions.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u-v)=\sin u\cos v-\cos u\sin v.
$$

The angle $\frac{4\pi}{3}=\pi+\frac{\pi}{3}$ is in quadrant III. Its reference angle is $\frac{\pi}{3},$ so

$$
\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)=-\frac{1}{2},\qquad
\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Substitute these values, keeping the subtraction from the difference formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin\left(x-\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)
&=\sin x\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)-\cos x\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)\\
&=\sin x\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)-\cos x\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first coefficient is $-\frac{1}{2}.$ The second is positive $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ because subtracting the negative sine value gives a plus.

The zero coefficient removes the $\sin x$ term; the surviving term is $\cos x.$

questions.:question/problem: Express $\sin\left(x+\pi\right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.

Use the sum formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v.
$$

The fixed angle has exact values

$$
\cos\left(\pi\right)=-1,\qquad \sin\left(\pi\right)=0.
$$

Substitute $u=x$ and $v=\pi$, then simplify the coefficients:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin\left(x+\pi\right)&=\sin x\cos\left(\pi\right)+\cos x\sin\left(\pi\right)\\

&=-\sin x.
\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_example.:question/problem: Express $\sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{6} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\sin(u+v) = \sin{u}\cos{v} + \cos{u}\sin{v}
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(x+\frac{\pi }{6}\right) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{6}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
